title: Analyzing the Training Dynamics of Image Restoration Transformers: A Revisit to Layer Normalization
claim: Standard normalization lets feature magnitudes explode and channel entropy collapse early in training, whereas the proposed variant stays stable and well-distributed.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, two 3D surface plots plus a 2D line close-up
description: Three side-by-side plots compare conventional LayerNorm with the proposed method during training. Panels (a) and (b) are 3D surface plots. Their axes are network layer and training iterations (in thousands). The jet colormap is shown on a colorbar at the left of each panel. In (a), the vertical axis is feature scale, up to 4e7. The 'Ours' surface is a flat blue sheet near zero. The 'LayerNorm' surface shoots up into a red spike at deep layers and late iterations. In (b), the vertical axis is entropy. The 'Ours' sheet stays flat and high, near 5. The 'LayerNorm' surface drops into a deep red valley. Labels are colored red for LayerNorm and blue for Ours. Panel (c) is a 2D line plot of entropy against iterations. The blue 'Ours' line stays near 5. The red LayerNorm line falls to zero within about 3K iterations. The eye goes first to the tall red spike and the deep valley.
caption: \textbf{Visualization of feature magnitudes and channel-wise entropy during training of an Image Restoration (IR) Transformer using conventional LayerNorm (LN) and \iln{} (Ours).} (a) Evolution of feature magnitudes across layers and training iterations, highlighting the dramatic divergence (to million-scale) under conventional LN. (b-c) Channel-wise entropy with LN drops sharply at the very early stage of training, indicating the emergence of acute peaks hidden in specific channels. Ours \iln{} exhibits well-distributed activation across channels and significant stability.
abstract: This work analyzes the training dynamics of Image Restoration (IR) Transformers and uncovers a critical yet overlooked issue: conventional LayerNorm (LN) drives feature magnitudes to diverge to a million scale and collapses channel-wise entropy. We analyze this in the perspective of networks attempting to bypass LN's constraints that conflict with IR tasks. Accordingly, we address two misalignments between LN and IR: 1) per-token normalization disrupts spatial correlations, and 2) input-independent scaling discards input-specific statistics. To address this, we propose Image Restoration Transformer Tailored Layer Normalization i-LN, a simple drop-in replacement that normalizes features holistically and adaptively rescales them per input. We provide theoretical insights and empirical evidence that this simple design effectively leads to both improved training dynamics and thereby improved performance, validated by extensive experiments.
